_note: Written by Claude at each refresh from `npm run build-aeo` output. Rules: no em or en dashes, no 'not X but Y' contrasts, only numbers the build prints, never invent recommendations (opportunity text comes from Peec), never rank topics against each other on raw visibility (Matt), Mutiny never framed as website personalization/CRO.
summary: First full week on the new Peec set (Oct 30 to Nov 5, 145 prompts, 29 brands). Mutiny is mentioned in 1.8% of AI answers (#24 of 29). The ladder shows where it breaks: AI engines read mutinyhq.com in 9.3% of chats and cite it in 2.5%, so our pages are part of the research and rarely make it into the answer. Week-over-week arrows start with the Nov 11 refresh.
brandFlags: Highspot (24.0%), Gong (23.7%) and Seismic (23.5%) lead overall. Highspot and Seismic score mostly on sales enablement; Gong scores across call recording, the AI GTM stack and AI sales assistants. The overall ranking mixes very different categories, so use the topic cards to compare Mutiny with the brands it actually meets in each conversation.

SE.competitive: Seismic (68.7%) and Highspot (67.0%) dominate; Showpad (46.3%) and Mindtickle (42.4%) follow. Mutiny is #10 at 3.0%.
SE.trend: The AI-native angle works: Mutiny is in 60.6% of answers for "AI-native Highspot alternative" and 51.5% for "AI-native Seismic alternative". Our Highspot alternatives page is a top-5 source for the plain "Highspot alternatives" prompt and still isn't getting us named.

DSR.competitive: Aligned (47.9%), Dock (41.9%) and Trumpet (41.7%) split the topic. Mutiny is #14 at 0.6%.
DSR.trend: Our "Best tools to create deal rooms" list is the #27 most-read URL across all six topics (49 chats, 12 citations). Mutiny shows up in 18.2% of answers for "How to create a deal room".

SPP.competitive: PandaDoc (26.1%), Qwilr (25.1%) and Gamma (24.8%) lead a crowded field. Mutiny is #10 at 3.8%.
SPP.trend: No brand passes 26.1% here, so the topic is still open. Mutiny already appears for "Best tool for personalized sales content" (27.3%), "AI-native sales content platform" (24.2%) and "AI agent that creates sales content" (21.2%).

GTM.competitive: Clay (50.9%) and Gong (47.7%) lead, Apollo.io follows at 34.8%. Mutiny is #21 at 0.6%.
GTM.trend: AI engines do read us here: mutinyhq.com is the #8 domain for this topic (57 chats) and is cited in 2.0% of them. Matt's warning applies to the broad prompts, which Clay's partner network makes very hard to move, so aim at niche ones.

CALL.competitive: Gong (56.3%), Fireflies (51.9%) and Avoma (48.0%) own call recording. Mutiny is #8 at 1.3%.
CALL.trend: Smallest topic (11 prompts). Our angle is what happens after the call: Mutiny shows up in 12.1% of answers for turning recordings into follow-up content.

ASA.competitive: Gong (34.7%) leads, then Clay (16.9%) and Apollo.io (15.3%). Mutiny is #16 at 0.2%.
ASA.trend: This is the category Mutiny now sells into and it's where Mutiny is weakest, so it stays the priority. The backlog anchor is "Sybill alternatives", where Sybill, Gong, Avoma and Fathom are each named in at least half the answers.

channels: ChatGPT mentions Mutiny most (2.9% of answers), then Perplexity (1.4%) and Google AI Overview (1.0%). Perplexity names Mutiny earliest when it does appear (average position 1.2, against 3.1 on Google AI Overview and 3.6 on ChatGPT).
domains: mutinyhq.com is the #11 most-read domain (283 chats) and is cited in 2.5% of chats. salesforce.com, youtube.com, hubspot.com, g2.com and highspot.com are what AI reads most for these topics; G2, YouTube and Reddit (#6) are the off-site sources Matt says carry weight.
outreach: Mutiny is on 3 of the top 50 URLs, and all 3 are our own pages (sales enablement guide #25, deal rooms list #27, AI sales tools guide #44). 14 of the other top-50 pages belong to challenger sites, the kind Matt says will swap inclusions. Start with GetAccept's digital sales room comparison (#2), Shiken (#8) and SpotSaaS (#12).
cro: The positioning watch is still the Oct 28 pull (90-day lookback): seven pages AI engines read call Mutiny a website personalization tool, led by two Warmly posts (129 and 76 retrievals). Correction emails for these sites are drafted in the Notion outreach tracker. This is Matt's priority 1.

takeaways: Fix positioning first (Matt's priority 1): CRO pages on mutinyhq.com are now redirected or noindexed, and correction emails to the third-party sites are drafted and waiting to be sent.

Turn reads into citations: mutinyhq.com is read in 9.3% of chats and cited in 2.5%. Refresh the pages AI already reads (sales enablement guide, deal rooms list, Highspot alternatives) with a 40 to 60 word answer under each H2 and an FAQ.
Lean on AI-native: Mutiny is in 60.6% of answers for "AI-native Highspot alternative" and 51.5% for "AI-native Seismic alternative", its two strongest prompts.
AI Sales Assistants is the category Mutiny sells into and Mutiny is at 0.2% there. Lead with niche prompts; Gong owns the broad ones.
Start the currency exchange: all 3 top-50 URLs that mention Mutiny are our own, and 14 challenger pages in the top 50 don't list Mutiny yet.

lean.SE: Position Mutiny as the AI-native option that creates on-brand assets for each deal. Describe Seismic and Highspot fairly on content management.
lean.DSR: Mutiny builds deal rooms from CRM, call and email context. Give Dock, Aligned and Trumpet the same depth.
lean.SPP: Mutiny generates proposals, decks and business cases for each deal. Credit PandaDoc, Qwilr and Gamma for their own strengths.
lean.GTM: Slot Mutiny into the sales asset and deal execution layer of the stack. Keep it out of any website personalization framing.
lean.CALL: Mutiny works after the call, turning recordings into follow-up content. Position it alongside Gong and Fireflies.
lean.ASA: Mutiny is an AI sales assistant for AEs that builds deal-specific content. Lead with the AE use case and name Gong, Clay and Apollo.io fairly.
